Cc: procurement@helios.ai, ops@helios.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Question on reserve sizing and GPU mix — Helios RFP HL-0667

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the RFP response. Procurement wants to lock a committed reservation window but we need a tight recommendation on how to bucket our workload and what GPU mix to commit to versus using burst capacity. Short background on our workload:
- Primary: low-latency chat (context up to 8k tokens), ~50 sustained RPS during business hours, spiky up to 180 RPS for 2-4 hours/day; p95 latency target 120ms for user-facing chat.
- Secondary: nightly batch reranking (avg 100k queries over 6 hours), throughput-focused with relaxed latency.
- Embeddings: continuous ingestion at ~8k vectors/hour (512-d), can be batched.

Questions:
1) Recommended baseline committed GPU types and counts for a 12-month reserved contract to meet the SLAs above while minimizing cost.
2) Guidance on burst lanes (how much headroom to reserve vs burst).
3) Any quantization/packing recommendations and failure/fallback guidance if a model upgrade increases memory needs.

We attached our estimate workbook (Helios_Reserve_Workbook_v1.xlsx) — appreciate a short write-up we can attach to procurement. Can you get back to us this week?

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Director of AI Platforms
Helios Labs

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on reserve sizing and GPU mix — Helios RFP HL-0667

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear breakdown. High-level summary up front: for your mix (latency-sensitive chat + batch + steady embeddings) we typically recommend a split between high-performance latency nodes (H100 family) and efficient throughput nodes (A100 80GB or mixed H100/A100 depending on model sizes), with L4-style nodes for small embedding workloads if you want further cost reduction.

Concrete baseline recommendation (12-month commitment):
- Latency pool (pinned): 4 H100-80GB GPUs exposed as a low-latency pool (expected served model family: 70B/30B-ish quantized at FP16/AMP). Estimated sustained capacity: 40–60 RPS for the 8k-context chat model when using our per-request KV cache + small batches (batch size 1–4). P95 latency ~90–130ms (depends on prompt length).
- Throughput pool (reserved): 8 A100-80GB GPUs for daytime batch and non-critical chat overflow. With packing and INT8 quantization suggestions this pool is expected to additionally handle your 100k nightly rerank within the 6-hour window plus burst overflow for user traffic.
- Embeddings: 1–2 L4-class GPUs (or a single A100 split slot) depending on concurrency; these are inexpensive and easily autoscaled/burstable.

Burst lane guidance:
- Recommend committing to 60–70% of your 95th-percentile steady need and using a 2x burst lane for spikes (automated burst policy for up to 6 hours/day, 4x for one-off incidents). This reduces committed spend while keeping predictable tail coverage. Example: if you see 50 sustained RPS baseline and 180 RPS peak, commit to sizing that covers ~120 RPS equivalent (60–70% baseline + steady headroom) and rely on burst for the remaining peaks.

Quantization and packing notes:
- Where possible use INT8/QLoRA-style quantization for A100-pool models to increase packing efficiency; reserve H100s for unquantized or large-context variants where latency is critical.
- Enable prefix KV caching for chat (cache common system+instruction prefixes) to cut per-request compute ~12–30% depending on prompt reuse.

Attachments: we pulled a starter workbook and a GPU fitment matrix (attached). Priyom / Laura — adding you for specifics on packing math and a succinct bullet list Maya can attach to procurement.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Maya — quick technical addendum with numbers you can paste into procurement: 

1) Packing and throughput examples (empirical):
- A100-80GB (INT8 / heavy packing): ~4500 generated tokens/sec per GPU for medium-context models (up to ~32k token/sec for short contexts when batching aggressively). For your nightly rerank workload we estimate 8 A100s will complete 100k rerank jobs comfortably within 6 hours if jobs are batched (batch size 64–128).
- H100-80GB (low-latency): ~120–180 RPS for 70B-family models at 8k context when using per-request batching=1–3 and KV cache enabled. We sized 4 GPUs to give 40–60 sustained RPS with headroom for transient spikes; if you need guaranteed 100 RPS steady, add +2 H100 GPUs.

2) Memory/overflow safeguards:
- Recommend a fallback policy to an A100 pool when H100 memory pressure crosses 85% (automated routing in the Redwood control plane). Also enable model-variant fallbacks (e.g., 70B->30B) with automatic quality gating to avoid errors during upgrades.

3) Costing heuristics to present to procurement:
- Commit to 60% baseline and provision a scheduled burst allowance (2x) — that typically lowers committed expense by ~25% vs committing to steady-peak.

Attachments: kv-cache-sizing-notes.txt has the assumptions used for KV cache hit rates and per-request memory delta.

- Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
